Recent indicators suggest solid real activity, but the Committee’s emphasis on “lack of further progress” toward 2 percent and its choice to hold rates while slowing QT is consistent with forecast-targeting and risk-management principles in Svensson and Woodford (2005) and with Taylor-rule style reaction functions adopted by the Fed. Anchoring inflation expectations—central in the New Keynesian Phillips Curve—justifies the cautious tone, echoing lessons from the Volcker disinflation and identification of policy shocks in Romer and Romer and Bernanke–Mihov. The slower Treasury runoff may modestly ease term-premium pressures (U.S. Treasury yields influence monetary policy), but the overall message remains cautiously hawkish despite balanced-risk language.
